newsitem.title: USA: Bond analysts troubled by disclosure, ask SEC meet.
newsitem.headline: Bond analysts troubled by disclosure, ask SEC meet.

text.p: The chairman of the National Federation of Municipal Analysts warned on Wednesday that some bond issuers are not complying with the letter or spirit of the SEC's municipal disclosure rule.

Jeff Baker, vice president of Chase Manhattan Bank, added that his group will meet with Securities and Exchange Commission officials on the matter shortly and is willing to hand over names of problem issuers at the session.
An SEC spokesperson confirmed that the agency will meet with analysts, but added that no date has been set.
"I would suspect that we know of at least 25 issuers" that are not complying, Baker said, adding most are issuers of health care bonds.

Approved in November 1994, the SEC's muni disclosure Rule 15c2-12 bars dealers from underwriting issues of muni securities unless the issuer pledges to provide notice of material events to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's continuing disclosure information system or to all nationally recognized municipal securities information repositories (NRMSIRs).
Baker outlined some of his concerns in a letter to analysts released on Wednesday.
"Recently, I have become aware of certain issuers who have not filed their annual financial statements and other material data with the NRMSIRs on a timely basis," he said.
"In addition, some issuers are refusing to directly provide analysts with their financial information," he said.
"Some issuers have told analysts/investors that they should get the requested documents from a NRMSIR," Baker said.
"Not only can this be an expensive proposition (about $25 per request), but it is a poor investor relations maneuver on the part of the issuer," Baker said.

"Certain bond counsels and financial advisers have recommended that issuers should provide the minimum as far as secondary market disclosure is concerned as long as they are in compliance with SEC Rule 15c2-12," Baker said.
"It is up to us to educate the issuer on the importance of providing financial and utilization data to the analytical community," he said.
Bond analysts in conjunction with the Public Securities Association will hold a seminar on the status of compliance with the SEC's disclosure rule next month, PSA said.
